text:
Anya: heads up — noticed a sharp drop in KV/prefix cache hit-rate for model:mosaic-7b in us-west-2 around 11:48 UTC, correlates with a 3x 95p latency reg.
Ben: timeline? any deploys around then?
Anya: last rollout was a small batching-heuristics tweak at 11:40 by infra-ci (autoscaler/batch-window reduced). infra metrics show prefix_cache.hit_rate went from ~82% -> 16% in ~5m.
Chi: noisy neighbor? GPU memory pressure?
Infra Bot: deploy: autoscaler-service v2.14.3 promoted by pipeline #452 at 11:39:52 UTC.
Dmitri: I pulled the serving runtime flamegraphs. Attaching snippet: ``````
# flamegraph excerpt (top functions)
serve::kv_cache::get_prefix -> 48% CPU
serve::batcher::enqueue -> 22% CPU
cuda::kernel_selector::choose -> 12% CPU
``````
Sam: interesting that kernel_selector shows up — could be fragmentation causing different kv keys?
Anya: logs show a sudden increase in unique cache keys (unique_prefix_count) from 1.2M -> 8.9M. That smells like cache key canonicalization changed.
Ben: any config that touches request hashing/normalization?
Chi: the batching-heuristics change included a toggle: `preserve_input_signature=true` for a new codepath. If that flips signature generation (adds batch-id to key) it would blow up cache.
Dmitri: found the exact commit — autoscaler PR 2017 added `preserve_input_signature` default true for GPU-batching prototypes. It was intended to keep shapes stable but I guess it mutated the signature builder.
Anya: if signature includes transient fields (batch_id, timestamp) that will poison the KV cache. Can we confirm with a sample request key?
Sam: pulled one of the malformed keys from logs: `prefix_key:v2|batch=7|ts=170000|user_sig=...` vs old `prefix_key:v1|user_sig=...`.
Ben: rollback plan? If we flip `preserve_input_signature=false` do we need restart? it's a config flag that threads read on startup.
Chi: quick mitigation: pin autoscaler back to v2.14.2 and restart pods in us-west-2 serving pool. That should restore canonical keys and let cached entries be reused.
Infra Bot: action created: INC-2026 KV cache hit-rate collapse — rollback autoscaler v2.14.3 to v2.14.2 (us-west-2) assigned to @Chi.
Dmitri: before rollback we should manually invalidate the worst offenders to free KV memory: `curl -X POST /admin/kv/invalidate?prefix=prefix_key:v2` — but be careful, invalidating everything could cause a cache warmup spike.
Anya: agreed — prefer rollback first, then targeted invalidations for `prefix_key:v2*`. I'll monitor hit-rate.
Ben: after rollback we should also add a unit test guarding that signature builder doesn't include ephemeral fields.
Sam: created a quick repro: sending two identical prompts with different batch ids produced different kv keys. Pasted minimal repro: ``````
# repro (python)
for i in [1,2]:
  req = {"prompt":"hello","batch_id":i}
  print(build_signature(req))
``````
Chi: rolling back now (starting drains and rolling update). ETA 4m for initial pods.
Anya: monitoring dashboards — prefix_cache.hit_rate climbing back to 74% at 11:57 UTC after first wave. 95p latency back to baseline ~130ms.
Dmitri: follow-ups: (1) add CI test that serializes signature builder output across typical request fields, (2) add a hist of unique_prefix_count per minute to detect sudden cardinality spikes, (3) make signature builder immutable to batch-level metadata.
Ben: also add an emergency circuit that refuses to accept signature schema changes without a compat flag.
Sam: noting postmortem action: PR author to add changelog entry and a short note in the release that `preserve_input_signature` touches cache keys.
Anya: thanks all. I'll update INC-2026 with timeline and mitigation.
Chi: one last note — kernel-selector churned because cache miss rate makes us hit small-seq kernels more often (cache misses -> full decode -> different seq lengths). That explains the kernel_selector presence in the profile.
Dmitri: good catch. closing loop: main root cause = signature canonicalization regression introduced in autoscaler v2.14.3, which poisoned prefix Kv cache and caused mass evictions and latency spike.
Anya: marking incident as mitigated, will move to postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
